subject.title: fix(ssrf): block loopback addresses for trusted hostname origins

question: Should this public external SSRF-boundary PR proceed after it is narrowed and proven, or should maintainers replace it with a separate security-owned patch?
rationale: SSRF policy is security-sensitive, and automation cannot decide whether this public contributor branch is the right security-handling path once proof is supplied.

options.title: Proceed after narrowing and proof
options.body: Keep the public PR open, require removal of the cron change plus redacted real runtime proof, then route to security-aware maintainer review before merge.

options.title: Replace with security-owned patch
options.body: Close or supersede this PR only after a maintainer-owned patch covers the same loopback rebinding gap with proof.

options.title: Pause until sponsorship
options.body: Leave the PR blocked until a security owner explicitly sponsors either the contributor branch or a replacement.

recommendation.title: Proceed after narrowing and proof
recommendation.body: Keep the public PR open, require removal of the cron change plus redacted real runtime proof, then route to security-aware maintainer review before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and merged the current security-sensitive SSRF code path this PR extends.
